title: No order-15 circulant has diameter 2 and monophonic position number 2
exact_endpoint: Circulant350979.source_refutation : ¬ Circulant350979.SourceClaim, where SourceClaim := ∀ n ≥ 11, ∃ J : Set (ZMod n), (circulantGraph J).diam = 2 ∧ mpNumber (circulantGraph J) = 2
scope: Tuite-Thomas-Chandran (arXiv:2106.06827v3; Ars Math. Contemp. 2025) Conjecture 4.5 asserts that for every n >= 11 there is a circulant graph of order n with diameter 2 and monophonic position number 2 (still listed as open in the survey arXiv:2501.19385 v5, August 2026). False at the interior order 15. Every diameter-2 circulant of order 15 contains a triangle, or is C5[3K1] (jumps {1,4,6} or {2,3,7}) with three open twins; both kinds of triple are mp-sets. Verified circulant examples exist at every other order 11..40 (supplementary; not claimed beyond).
source_targets: J. Tuite, E. J. Thomas, U. Chandran S. V., arXiv:2106.06827v3 Conjecture 4.5
substantive_reason: It refutes a human-posed published conjecture, which a 2026 survey still lists as open, at an interior order, with a universal nonexistence theorem over all order-15 circulants and a structural explanation (triangle or C5 blow-up twins). It is not an endpoint, convention or wording correction, and it is not derivable from the source's lemmas. Modest significance, consistent with the 355140 and 349441 precedents.
